value.body: A choreographer designs dance movement and teaches it to performers, for stage productions, films, music videos, weddings, events and competitions. Many start as assistant choreographers in a team. A typical day involves planning movement to music, running rehearsals and adjusting the piece with directors or clients.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BPA in Dance, or years of training in a dance form

items.label: Students in B.P.A. (Bachelor of Performing Arts)
items.note: All performing arts (dance, music, theatre); all years, all modes. Counts only institutions that responded to AISHE, so national totals may be higher.

items.label: Students in M.P.A. (Master of Performing Arts)
items.note: All years, all modes. Counts only institutions that responded to AISHE, so national totals may be higher.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most choreographers begin as dancers or assistants to an established choreographer, building a reel of their own work. Film and TV work usually needs membership of a dancers' or choreographers' association in that industry.

value.title: At a glance
items: Income depends on a steady flow of projects and contacts.
Teaching classes alongside is a common way to keep income steady.
Next roles: lead choreographer, studio owner, creative director for shows.
